title: The 1787 Constitution vests granted legislative powers in Congress
summary: The 1787 Constitution vests granted legislative powers in Congress.
body: Article I, Section 1 of the National Archives transcription of the 1787 Constitution vests the legislative powers the Constitution grants in a Congress of two houses. The source says: "All legislative Powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States, which shall consist of a Senate and House of Representatives." The sentence covers powers 'herein granted,' not every power a government might exercise. Later amendments are not part of the transcription page opened for this card.
